newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Allstate to improve auto growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Allstate to improve auto growth.

text.p: Allstate Corp will turn its attention to improving premium growth in its standard and preferred auto insurance businesses in 1997, Allstate chief executive Jerry Choate said.
"I think we have a challenge in one place and that's standard and preferred auto," Choate said in an interview with Reuters.
"We're going to accelerate the new business growth," he said. "Certainly, we have all the capital we need to do it."
Allstate said it could not provide premium growth figures for the standard and preferred auto businesses in the fourth quarter of 1996.
Meanwhile, Northbrook, Ill.-based Allstate also said it has a goal of increasing consolidated revenue by about eight percent, up from 6.6 percent in 1996.
But the company said it does not expect to achieve that target in 1997.
In the standard and preferred auto insurance businesses, Choate said he hopes to achieve better growth this year through improved market segmentation and pricing.
"That should help us a fair amount," Choate said.
Increased production from an expanded agency force also should help improve premium growth, Choate said.
Allstate also expects to increase promotion and advertising for those lines of business, he said.
"We're going to put a full court press on the auto business," he said.
Allstate, the second largest U.S. personal lines insurer, also expects to return to the California market aggressively in 1997.
"We're going to very aggressively go after that market," he said. "The biggest market in the country is going to have Allstate back in the middle of it," he said.
Allstate also is now fairly comfortable with its catastrophe exposure in the homeowners markets in California and Florida, Choate said.
He said the New York area is now the only remaining region where catastrophe exposures are too high.
But, he said, the company plans to just gradually decrease its exposure there, rather than take any kind of drastic measures.
"We're bringing that down at a slower pace," he said. "The likelihood of a major hurricane there is really slim."
Meanwhile, Allstate is currently very well capitalized and is considering how to use any excess capital, Choate said.
Allstate in November said its board of directors authorized the expansion of its stock repurchase plan by up to $750 million through the end of 1997.
Choate said the company is considering all its options, but did not rule out the possibility of future acquisitions.

"We would consider all options, really," he said. An acquisition, he said, would have to be a good strategic fit with Allstate. "We aren't going to acquire something just to acquire it. We're doing pretty well in the marketplace without acquiring anything else," he said.
But, "If we had something that fit and made sense, we would consider it," he said.
Allstate earlier reported fourth quarter operating earnings of $1.15 a share compared with analysts' First Call consensus estimate of $1.10 a share.
